3.– WORKSHEET: CRAZY CHARACTERS (P.10) (8’)
Crazy Characters
10
MATERIALS
•	 Pencils or crayons
NOTE: if you collected your Ss books during the booklet 
activity, have them ask you for it now by saying, “Can I have 
my book please?”; otherwise, ask them to take it out of their 
bag. Explain the activity before giving out the books/asking Ss 
to take them out since they might get distracted.
This worksheet shows three characters at the top of the page, 
and a variety of facial features in the bottom half. Ss must mark 
with an X the features of each character that are incorrect and 
draw a line to the bottom of the page to the correct feature.
Review the target structure by pointing to one of the S and 
asking their classmates for example, “Look, John has got blue 
hair.”. Ss should answer by correcting you, “No, that’s wrong. 
John hasn’t got blue hair; he has got brown hair.” Do this a 
couple more times with other Ss.
Show them the worksheet and say, “Look! Dad, Pam, and 
Paul look very different today! What’s wrong?”. Then, point to 
the picture of Dad and ask, “Has Dad got a small mouth?” and 
the Ss must reply, “No, he hasn’t. Dad has got a big mouth.”. 
Make sure all Ss repeat the structure. Then have them draw 
an “X” on Dad’s mouth and draw a line to the correct mouth 
pictured at the bottom of the page. 
KEY
Dad hasn’t got a small mouth, he has got a big mouth. 
Paul hasn’t got brown eyes, he has got green eyes. 
Pam hasn’t got red hair, she has got brown hair. 
NOTE: only complete page 10, page 11 is for a different day.

> Scenario A
If your group has achieved the activity goal on My Way (i.e., 
they have done all or most of the activities in the current Mission), 
say, “You’re doing amazing on My Way! You have played lots 
of games in Mission 3, so we can do a special sticker activity 
together!”. Take the Day 7 stickers and have them ask, “Can I 
have some stickers, please?”. Do the activity as instructed below. 
> Scenario B
If your group hasn’t reached the activity goal on My Way, 
simply move on with the class. You will have to complete one 
or two activities from the bonus section to make up for the 
time allotted to this dynamic.
The point of this activity is to practise clothes vocabulary in a 
fun way. These two pages contain three different dynamics, but 
we will focus on the dynamic on the top and middle row. Ss have 
to stick the wardrobe and character stickers and identify what is 
missing in the character’s wardrobe based on the description. 
Model the task by looking for the stickers, sticking them, and 
answering the questions.

Have Ss open pp.22-23 (sticker section) and say, “Let’s 
see what is missing in the characters’ wardrobes!”. Point 
to rectangle number 55 and ask, “What number is this?”. Ss 
should respond, “It’s number 55!”. Say, “Can you find number 
55 on the sticker sheet?” and elicit, “Here it is!”. Then read 
the description of grandma’s wardrobe in the middle of the 
page, and ask, “What’s missing?” while pointing to the clothing 
items on the page, to which your Ss should reply, “The gold 
slippers are missing!”
Follow the same procedure for Pam (in this case you will 
have to stick sticker 62 as well) and Mum. If time allows, do 
the other characters’ wardrobes as well. If you can’t finish the 
whole activity, tell the Ss that they can continue at home.
We recommend making this activity more dynamic by turning 
it into a competition to answer the questions as fast as possible. 
You can give points to Ss who respond correctly.

Sticker 55: The gold slippers are missing from Grandma’s 
wardrobe.

Sticker 60: The brown jumper is missing from Grandpa’s

6.– PAM&PAUL BOARD GAME (14’)
P.E.M.4.1
START
FINISH
P.E.M.4
Play as many rounds of the Pam&Paul Board Game as time 
allows.

SET-UP
1.	 The game can be played individually or in groups (this is 
recommended for big groups). Each player/pair chooses 
a counter and places it on the start square.
2.	 Start the game using one of the strategies in the “Starting 
a game” section in the introduction of the TG. 
3.	 Have them roll the dice and move their counter. Depending 
on the colour of the square (category) the Ss land on, ask 
them to perform the challenge mentioned in the Board 
Game Reference Sheet. 
Special squares:
•	 Square with a plane on it: follow the dotted line and 
go back to the start.
•	 Square with Billy on it: follow Billy’s footprints and 
do the challenge.
•	 Square with a bicycle on it: ride down the road and 
do the challenge.
4.	 If they perform the challenge correctly, they can stay 
on the square. If not, give them a second chance by 
rewording or giving them clues. If they still can’t get it, 
they go back to the square they were in before.
5.	 The game ends when someone reaches the finish line.
7.– ACTIVITY 4: PLAY DETECTIVE (7’)
> How to Play
One S is the detective and has to wait outside the classroom 
while another S (the thief) takes the Purse cutout and hides it 
by putting in their pocket or sitting on it. The detective has to 
find out who the thief is by asking questions.
> Main Activity
Introduce the activity by saying, “Let’s see if the detective 
can find the thief!”
Choose a thief, have them hide the purse, and tell the detective 
to come back into the room. Use the structure: “Detective,

detective, come in!”. The detective should ask questions to 
the group to find out who has the purse.
Before starting the round, the group can say, “What does the 
thief look like?” (they can sing this part). Then the detective 
can start asking yes or no questions such as:
•	 Has the thief got long hair?
•	 Is the thief wearing black shoes?
•	 Is the thief tall or short?
Always insist that the Ss ask and answer questions in full 
sentences and structures. Discourage the Ss from asking 
whether the thief was a boy or a girl unless they really can’t 
figure out who the thief is, because doing so may make guessing 
who the thief is too easy. 
When the detective is ready to guess, they should ask, “John, 
are you the thief?” and the S being accused should respond, 
“Yes, I am.” or “No, I am not.” If the detective accuses somebody 
wrongly, the thief wins; if the detective accuses somebody and 
their guess is correct, then they win.
> Variation
Once Ss are comfortable playing this game, you can bring 
in some props and have the Ss wear different accessories like 
hats and glasses to make it more fun. This way the detective 
can ask a greater variety of questions.

9.– TIME TO GO HOME (TR#20) (2’)
Sing the Time to Go Home song and have the Ss form a line

BONUS
ACTIVITY 1: MAKE A FACE (VERSION 3)
P.3.1
> Main Activity
Tell your Ss, “It’s time to meet a new friend!”. Use Blu-Tack 
to place the A3 sheet on the whiteboard. Ask your Ss, “What 
is this person’s name?”, and have them choose a name for 
the character. You can write it on the A3 using an erasable 
whiteboard marker.
Each number on the dice corresponds with a face part. Ss 
take turns rolling the dice and choosing one characteristic for 
the character based on the number. They have to answer the 
corresponding question and place the cutout on the A3. 
Here is the target language depending on the number they get:
Hair
T: What is her/his hair like?
S: He/she has got … hair.
Eyes
T: What are her/his eyes like?
S: He/she has got … eyes.
Nose
T: What is her/his nose like?
S: He/she has got a big/small nose.
Mouth
T: What is her/his mouth like?
S: He/she has got a big/small mouth.
Moustache
T: Has he/she got a moustache?
S: Yes. He/she has got a moustache. / 
No. He/she hasn’t got a moustache. 
Ears
T: What are her/his ears like? 
S: He/she has got big/small ears.

ACTIVITY 8: HOW OLD ARE YOU?
P.3.2
Lisa
P.3.8
15
Lisa
> Main Activity
Ss must guess the age of the different characters. Prepare 
two sets of cards, one with the character’s age (P.3.8) and one 
without (P.3.2). Choose a pair of cards of the same character, 
keep the age card in your hand and put the character card 
face up on the table for the Ss to see. Introduce the activity by 
saying, “Let’s see if you can guess how old the characters are!”
If you take the Nancy card, for example, you can start by 
asking, “How old is Nancy?” and Ss must take it in turns asking, 
“Is she 20 years old?”, for example. You should then respond, 
“No, she isn’t.” and encourage Ss to ask, “Is she younger or 
older?” to which you should respond “She is older.”. When they 
are ready to guess the character’s age, they should ask, “Is she 
… years old?”. Once the Ss have guessed correctly, show the 
card with the age of the character and let one of the Ss have 
a turn at choosing a card.
